title: Civil Services (IAS/IPS via UPSC)

path.duration: Most serious aspirants prepare for 2–5 years
path.note: Up to 6 attempts for general category (more for reserved categories).

pay.title: 7th Pay Commission

rows.label: Entry (Level 10)
rows.value: ₹56,100/month basic; with ~60% DA that's ~₹89,760 before HRA and other allowances

rows.label: Senior
rows.value: Rises through pay levels with promotions

notes: The 8th Pay Commission report is expected around 2027.
Plus housing, vehicle, staff and job security, which is a big part of the real value.

pros: Huge impact on people's lives and real power to fix problems
Unmatched social respect and job security
Variety: postings across districts, ministries and sectors
cons: About 1 seat for every ~800 applicants; most aspirants never get selected
Years of preparation with no income and big social pressure ("Abhi tak nahi hua?")
Transfers, political pressure, long hours and little control over where you live
Pay is modest compared with private-sector peers in the early years

competitionReality.signal: 8,19,372 applied for UPSC CSE 2026; ~5.49 lakh appeared
competitionReality.reality: 1,016 vacancies, so about 1 post for every ~800 applicants

sceneIdeas: A relative asks "what's your backup plan?" at a wedding
First posting as SDM, with a flood alert and a local politician on the phone at the same time
A coaching fee vs. family savings conversation
